Folks — drafting suggestions below for insertion into MSA/Order Form. I kept it pragmatic to avoid scaring procurement: 

1) Notice window: propose 30 days from receipt of written notice to provide Redwood with a written claim notice and reasonable information to investigate; if Customer fails to provide notice within 30 days, Redwood's right to indemnify is not automatically forfeited but Redwood's ability to defend may be hampered and the parties will use best efforts to cooperate.

2) Evidence custody: recommend we accept a customer-provided evidence bundle uploaded to a mutually-accessible S3 bucket (read-only for Redwood) + an evidence_matrix spreadsheet listing log files, sample prompts, and timestamps. Redwood will not require transfer of IP ownership — only copies sufficient to investigate. If litigation requires originals, Redwood will request custodial access via a court order or mutual agreement and will reimburse reasonable collection costs.

3) Defense control: push for right-to-defend for Redwood for third-party IP claims subject to standard carveouts (no settlement without Customer consent for claims that would materially affect Customer rights). If Customer insists on right-to-control, propose a hybrid option: Redwood can assume defense but Customer can take over if they provide additional indemnity/security.

I attached a short markup (msa_defend_vs_reimburse_markups.docx) and a proposed clause wording below. If Ben thinks 30 days is a non-starter commercialy, we can compromise at 45.

Kimberly Park
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference
